Friends must have identical enemy sets, so the friendship graph is a disjoint union of cliques and the enemy graph is complete multipartite with equal part sizes $s$. Each guest then has $n - s = 12$ enemies, so $s = n - 12$, and $s$ must divide $n$, which forces $s \mid 12$. This gives $n \in \{13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 24\}$, whose sum is 100.
